verdict.rationale: Devin Handoff lets a developer move a local task into a cloud session. That session runs on its own VM and keeps going after the laptop closes, and the web interface lets users follow and take over the work in an embedded IDE. This is the core of cross-device continuity, but no source says a session started on one device can be resumed from a different device or browser. missing for 10: explicit documentation of resuming a session from another device/browser, session sync/persistence details across clients, independent hands-on corroboration

support.subject: As a developer, I can start a task on one device and continue it later from another device or browser

citations.quote: The cloud session gets its own VM with a shell, browser, and full repo access, so it can keep going after you close your laptop.
Hand a task off to a cloud Devin session and keep working locally.
allows you to follow and take over Devin's development process in the embedded IDE.
